question: Can Haiku 5.5 with a typed reply answer the closed-set questions over the last 12 prompts?
why: The same questions as extract/haiku-typed on claude-haiku-5-5: does the newer, cheaper small model hold the same accuracy? It decides the model for the typed call and the cost.
hypothesis: Haiku 5.5 is at least as accurate as Haiku 4.5 on the closed-set questions, at a lower price.
cost_estimate: about 0.5M Haiku tokens like extract/haiku-typed, at Haiku 5.5 prices ($0.10 / $0.50 per million input / output); expect about 185 typed calls per run (110 on the sample, 74 on syn1)

deviations.what: Amendment A3 (Yotam, 2026-11-11): the Haiku 5.5 comparison is a new case, extract/haiku55-typed. Same questions, same pipeline, same datasets (syn1, then the A2 seeded sample of anon-personas: 20 personas, seed 20261110), config model claude-haiku-5-5. Bars copied unchanged from the test-tree row as registered in extract/haiku-typed.
deviations.cost: Token costs of extract/haiku-typed were measured before the stdin fix on lab/core (headless thinking leaked on about 2/3 of its calls), so cost is not comparable across the two cases; accuracy is. Haiku 5.5 price comes from the lab's price table (A3: $0.10 / $0.50 per million tokens).

deviations.from: test tree row: syn2 and real1
deviations.what: Amendment A1 replaces syn2 with anon-personas (kind real, anonymized); Amendment A2 maps the row: every bar the row puts on syn2 applies to anon-personas, and the real1 aggregates (run_agreement) are computed on the same anon-personas runs, numbers only. As a model case it runs the A2 seeded sample of anon-personas, the same one as reverify/heldout-personas: sample_dataset anon-personas, sample_size 20, sample_seed 20261110, random.Random(seed).sample(sorted(user_ids), 20). syn1 stays as the reference, reported beside, never alone.
deviations.cost: Running all 188 personas of anon-personas would cost about 9x the planned budget.
deviations.labels: Labels on anon-personas were written by headless Claude and are not human-reviewed (A2, decision 1): every verdict carries the caveat 'labels not human-reviewed'.
deviations.agg: The row names no aggregation for over_inferred, first_session_fill and run_agreement, so each uses the default, mean; slot_accuracy has both bars the row names (mean and min). run_agreement is a cross-run metric: the verdict reads it at run 3.
deviations.typed: Strategy hybrid_haiku (HaikuTypedClient, P/typed.py): one structured call per turn over the last 12 prompts, on claude-haiku-5-5 through headless Claude Code. The case pipeline wraps the replay StrategyPipeline so that, as for hybrid_jev, the learner's tap on each proposal is simulated and typed calls are counted as typed_questions; it changes no scoring and no strategy code.
